paragraphs: Liquid democracy lets people either vote directly or pass their voting weight to someone they trust. Because delegations can continue through several people, they can also form cycles. Ranked delegations address this complication by letting voters list several possible delegates in preference order. A delegation rule then determines how those preferences translate into representation.

Earlier work identified a trade-off between two desirable properties, anonymity and copy-robustness. This paper studies fractional delegation rules, which allow voting weight to be distributed rather than assigned entirely to one representative. It examines Mixed Borda branching and a random walk rule, each connected to one side of the earlier trade-off. Using the Markov chain tree theorem, the authors prove that these apparently different rules are equivalent and satisfy generalized versions of both properties.

The paper also makes the rule computationally usable. Combining that theorem with Fulkerson's algorithm yields a polynomial-time procedure for calculating the outcome. The contribution therefore joins a compatibility result for fractional delegation with an efficient computation method that also has applications in semi-supervised learning and graph theory.
neurips-2023-anonymous-and-copy-robust-d.tldr: Two fractional delegation rules are proved equivalent, jointly satisfying generalized anonymity and copy-robustness while permitting polynomial-time computation.

paragraphs: Generating a plausible program is only part of programming: users also need to revise it when its behavior misses their intent. ANPL addresses this interaction problem by giving users a structured way to divide a program into precise code and pieces described in natural language. The system also accepts input-output examples that the resulting program must satisfy.

Its organizing idea is a program sketch. The sketch specifies control and data flow, while designated holes contain submodules for a language model to implement. Users can change the sketch, rewrite a hole's description, or add examples for a particular hole. A hole can itself become another ANPL program, allowing the same process to repeat at a smaller scale. This makes local debugging possible without handing the rest of the program back to the model.

On ARC, ANPL outperforms programming baselines lacking interactive decomposition or guarantees about composing modules correctly. Evaluations on APPS, HumanEval, and practical programming tasks support its applicability across multiple domains. The released ARC solutions additionally document how people break unfamiliar tasks into programmable pieces.
neurips-2023-anpl-towards-natural-progra.tldr: ANPL combines precise program sketches, natural-language submodules, and examples so users can recursively refine and debug generated code.

paragraphs: Image retrieval needs a useful measure of similarity, but it also benefits from knowing when that measure is uncertain. This paper develops a Bayesian encoder for metric learning that represents uncertainty through a distribution over the network's weights. It constructs that distribution using a Laplace approximation, rather than the neural amortization approach used in earlier work.

The authors first establish a probabilistic interpretation of the training objective: contrastive loss can be understood as a negative log-likelihood on a spherical space. This result connects the similarity-learning objective to the probabilistic machinery used by their method. They also propose three ways to ensure that the covariance matrix is positive definite and introduce a decomposition of the Generalized Gauss-Newton approximation. These are mathematical components supporting the proposed weight-distribution approach.

The resulting Laplacian Metric Learner, or LAM, is evaluated for both prediction and uncertainty. The authors report well-calibrated uncertainty estimates, reliable detection of examples outside the training distribution, and state-of-the-art predictive performance. Together, these empirical findings suggest that uncertainty estimation can accompany strong retrieval predictions in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-bayesian-metric-learning-fo.tldr: LAM uses a Laplace approximation over encoder weights to deliver strong metric-learning predictions with empirically calibrated uncertainty.

paragraphs: Training one object detector on many datasets requires it to learn their particular characteristics while combining their knowledge. A previous approach uses a shared backbone with separate detection heads, but this substantially increases the number of parameters. DAMEX explores mixture-of-experts modeling as a way to organize dataset-specific knowledge inside a single detector.

The method trains routing behavior so that tokens from a dataset go to its assigned expert. This encourages experts to specialize according to the datasets contributing to training. The central idea is that a mixture of experts can serve a purpose beyond increasing model scale: it can explicitly accommodate differences among the data sources that a universal detector must learn from.

On the Universal Object-Detection Benchmark, DAMEX improves average AP by 10.2 over the existing state of the art and by 2.0 over the authors' non-MoE baseline. The reported gains also persist when mixing datasets with limited data, different domains, or differing label sets. Qualitative results further indicate resistance to expert representation collapse, supporting the intended specialization of the experts.
neurips-2023-damex-dataset-aware-mixture.tldr: DAMEX routes dataset tokens to specialized experts within one detector, improving object detection across mixtures of diverse datasets.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to learn the Kalman gain, the optimal filtering policy for a linear system, when the noise covariance matrices are unknown. Instead of starting with those noise statistics, the method learns from noisy system outputs. The objective is to choose a filtering policy that minimizes error in predicting those outputs.

The authors formulate this as stochastic policy optimization, connecting data-driven optimal filtering with its dual problem, optimal control. They analyze stochastic gradient descent for this formulation while explicitly accounting for biased gradients and stability constraints. Those considerations matter because the learning procedure must be understood as part of a dynamical filtering problem, rather than only as an unconstrained numerical optimization.

The analysis combines linear-system theory with high-dimensional statistics to separate error into bias and variance contributions. The resulting bounds scale logarithmically with the problem dimension. Another stated distinction from subspace methods is that output-trajectory length affects only the bias term. The contribution is therefore a theoretical account of both convergence and statistical error for learning a filter directly from noisy observations.
neurips-2023-data-driven-optimal-filteri.tldr: The paper analyzes learning a Kalman gain from noisy outputs, deriving convergence guarantees and bias-variance bounds without known noise covariances.

paragraphs: Synthesizing a new viewpoint from a single-camera video becomes difficult when scenes are uncontrolled or recordings are long. Existing approaches can also require substantial training for each new scene. DynPoint addresses these issues by organizing information around explicit three-dimensional relationships between neighboring frames, rather than encoding the entire video into a latent scene representation.

The method estimates depth and scene flow consistently across frames to predict those relationships. It then uses the resulting correspondences to gather information from several reference frames into a target frame. Hierarchical neural point clouds provide the representation for this aggregation. The approach therefore makes cross-frame correspondence the central mechanism for bringing together the information needed to render a requested view.

The authors report training acceleration typically around an order of magnitude while obtaining results comparable to earlier approaches. They also report strong robustness on long videos without learning a canonical representation of the video content. These findings support explicit correspondence and point-based aggregation as an effective route to faster view synthesis in the evaluated dynamic-video settings.
neurips-2023-dynpoint-dynamic-neural-poi.tldr: DynPoint aggregates video frames through explicit 3D correspondences and neural point clouds, typically reducing training time by an order of magnitude.

paragraphs: Forecasting several time series requires understanding both relationships between variables and dependencies across time. Many graph-based approaches assign these jobs to separate graph and temporal networks. FourierGNN instead treats them as one graph-modeling problem, motivated by the difficulty of coordinating two architectures and separating relationships that are intertwined in the data.

The authors introduce a hypervariate graph in which every individual observation is a node, regardless of its variable or timestamp. A sliding window becomes a fully connected graph spanning variables and time together. FourierGNN processes this representation by stacking Fourier Graph Operators that perform matrix multiplications in Fourier space. Its theoretical analysis establishes an equivalence between these operators and graph convolutions in the time domain.

This construction aims to retain expressive joint modeling while reducing computational complexity. Across seven datasets, the authors report better forecasting performance, higher efficiency, and fewer parameters than state-of-the-art methods. The findings support the paper's central proposal: one graph architecture can model the combined dependencies needed for forecasting without a separate temporal network.
neurips-2023-fouriergnn-rethinking-multi.tldr: FourierGNN models variables and timestamps in one graph and uses Fourier-space operators for accurate, efficient multivariate forecasting.

paragraphs: Comparing Bayesian optimization methods for combinatorial and mixed-variable problems is difficult when papers use different benchmarks and change several algorithmic components at once. Even a contribution targeting one component may be compared against systems with different surrounding components. The implementation work needed for controlled comparisons has helped perpetuate this problem.

This paper introduces a modular framework that makes Bayesian optimization components easier to combine and supplies diverse synthetic and practical benchmark tasks. Its flexibility allows the authors to implement 47 new combinations of MCBO components. They compare these against seven existing MCBO solvers and five standard black-box optimization algorithms on ten tasks, running more than 4,000 experiments.

The experiments identify a combination that outperforms existing approaches in the benchmark study. They also highlight the importance of model fit and using a trust region. Beyond the particular winning combination, the framework makes it easier to assess which component choices contribute to performance while keeping the rest of an algorithm consistent. The authors release the library under the MIT license.
neurips-2023-framework-and-benchmarks-fo.tldr: A modular MCBO library enables controlled benchmarking and identifies effective component combinations across more than 4,000 experiments.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation trains a smaller student model using a teacher model, but the design of that transfer process often depends on expert choices. A design that works for one pairing may be less suitable when the models differ in capacity or architecture. KD-Zero makes the distiller itself the object of an automated evolutionary search.

The framework separates a distiller into three components: transformations of knowledge, functions measuring distance, and weights for the losses. It builds a search space from operations for these components, then evolves candidate populations through crossover and mutation. Sharpness and the representation gap serve as fitting objectives. Loss rejection, a shrinking search space, and proxy settings are used to make the search more efficient.

The discovered distiller is then used for the final teacher-to-student transfer. Across diverse architectures and classification, detection, and segmentation tasks, the authors report consistent improvements over other state-of-the-art methods. Their analysis of the discovered designs also yields practical design insights. The evidence supports automatically adapting the transfer mechanism to the pairing, rather than relying entirely on a fixed handcrafted recipe.
neurips-2023-kd-zero-evolving-knowledge-.tldr: KD-Zero evolves distillation components automatically and reports improved teacher-to-student transfer across diverse architectures and visual tasks.

paragraphs: Vision Transformers can be costly because processing an image requires substantial computation. Many compression methods still divide the image at one fixed level of detail. MG-ViT starts from the observation that useful information often concentrates in a few regions, motivating a system that can allocate finer processing to important parts of an image.

Its two-stage procedure first divides the image into a small number of patches for a simple inference pass. When necessary, it proceeds to a second stage that subdivides important patches into smaller pieces. This creates a representation with multiple levels of detail and balances prediction performance against computation. The authors also extend the strategy to hierarchical Vision Transformers for detection and segmentation, broadening its use beyond classification.

Experiments support the effectiveness of this selective refinement. On ImageNet, the authors report reducing FLOPs by 47% for LV-ViT-S and 56% for DeiT-S without a performance loss. These results show that, for the reported models and setting, choosing where to increase image detail can substantially reduce arithmetic work while maintaining predictive performance.
neurips-2023-mg-vit-a-multi-granularity-.tldr: MG-ViT selectively refines important image patches, cutting reported ImageNet FLOPs substantially without sacrificing performance.

paragraphs: Recalibrating a classifier should make its probabilities reliable while preserving their predictive usefulness. This paper brings calibration and sharpness into one framework based on decomposing mean-squared error. The resulting notion of minimum-risk recalibration evaluates the balance between these goals, rather than treating reliable probabilities and informative predictions as separate concerns.

The authors apply this framework to uniform-mass binning, which recalibrates predictions through bins. With B bins and n samples, they derive a finite-sample risk upper bound of order B/n plus 1/B², up to logarithmic factors. Balancing these terms gives an optimal bin count scaling as n to the one-third power and an approximately n to the minus two-thirds risk bound. This provides a principled connection between available data and binning resolution.

The paper also considers label shift and proposes a two-stage adjustment using limited labeled target-domain data. Its results show that transferring an already calibrated classifier requires significantly fewer target samples than recalibrating from scratch. Numerical simulations support the tightness of the bounds, the bin-count choice, and the effectiveness of the adaptation procedure.
neurips-2023-minimum-risk-recalibration-.tldr: A minimum-risk framework balances calibration and sharpness, deriving binning guarantees and a sample-efficient approach to label-shift adaptation.

paragraphs: Large eddy simulation models turbulent flow while accounting for the effects of smaller scales. Ideal LES treats each full-resolution trajectory as a random realization of underlying dynamics and marginalizes small-scale effects to obtain deterministic evolution of the LES state. This formulation is analytically intractable, motivating a learned way to approximate its underlying stochastic description.

The proposed niLES framework uses a latent neural stochastic differential equation to model the evolving stochastic process. An encoder and decoder connect that latent representation to the desired ideal flow field. This differs from neural closure approaches that treat every trajectory as a deterministic realization. The distinction matters because the framework explicitly builds the randomness of full-order trajectories into its modeling approach.

The authors evaluate niLES on Kolmogorov flow at Reynolds number 20,000 and flow around a cylinder at Reynolds number 500. They report more accurate trajectory statistics and improved stability compared with competing methods, especially over long rollouts. The framework also accommodates non-uniform geometries through unstructured meshes, supporting its use across the tested flow configurations.
neurips-2023-neural-ideal-large-eddy-sim.tldr: niLES combines ideal large eddy simulation with a latent neural SDE to improve turbulence statistics and long-rollout stability.

paragraphs: As NAND flash memory stores more information, errors in writing and reading data become a greater challenge. This paper tackles reliability by learning how information bits should be translated into programming operations for individual memory cells. The goal is to reduce programming errors while also compensating for degradation as the memory ages.

The authors build a neural modulator around an autoencoder, with a model of the flash-memory channel placed between its encoder and decoder. A conditional generative adversarial network learns that channel model. Embedding the channel inside the learning architecture allows the writing scheme to be optimized with the modeled behavior of the memory in the loop. Generative and unsupervised learning thus contribute directly to how data are written.

When optimized for the end-of-life operating point, the learned system improves raw bit error rate over prior art by up to 56% and extends flash-block lifetime by up to 25%. These are reported maximum improvements under that optimization setting. They indicate that adapting the programming scheme to the channel can benefit both data reliability and usable memory lifetime.
neurips-2023-neural-modulation-for-flash.tldr: A learned flash-memory writing scheme reports up to 56% improvement in raw bit error rate and 25% longer block lifetime.

paragraphs: Sharpness-aware minimization, or SAM, is a training method intended to reduce the sharpness of learned minima and improve generalization. Its adversarial step perturbs model parameters. This paper asks how much of that perturbation is actually needed and finds that concentrating it on a very small, specific subset can improve performance.

The subset consists of the affine parameters in normalization layers, typically about 0.1% of all parameters. Perturbing only these parameters can outperform perturbing the entire model. The authors observe this behavior across different SAM variants and in both ResNets with Batch Normalization and Vision Transformers with Layer Normalization. The finding concerns which parameters receive the adversarial perturbation, rather than a claim that the rest of the network can be discarded.

Alternative sparse perturbation strategies do not achieve similar gains at such extreme sparsity in the comparisons reported. This points to a special role for normalization parameters in the observed effect. The results reaffirm SAM's generalization benefits while questioning whether reduced sharpness alone explains them; they do not establish that sharpness has no role.
neurips-2023-normalization-layers-are-al.tldr: Perturbing only normalization parameters during SAM can outperform full-parameter perturbation, challenging a sharpness-only explanation of its benefits.

paragraphs: This paper improves theoretical guarantees for stochastic mirror descent when learning linear predictors with quadratically bounded losses. That loss class includes both Lipschitz and smooth functions and covers regression and classification. The analysis addresses realizable and non-realizable problems, with data sampled either independently or from a Markov chain.

Earlier analysis coupled the original optimization iterates to another sequence projected into a bounded domain. Although this made standard concentration tools available, its use of a union bound across iterations contributed to weaker guarantees. The new approach directly analyzes the moment generating function of a specially constructed supermartingale sequence. This lets the proof use the structure of stochastic mirror descent more directly.

The authors obtain better high-probability generalization bounds across the settings studied. For realizable problems and non-realizable problems with light-tailed sub-Gaussian data, they remove a log T factor, reaching the stated rates of 1/T and 1/√T respectively. For heavy-tailed polynomial data, the improvement is a polynomial factor in T. These are sharper guarantees for the learning procedure, rather than empirical claims about a newly proposed predictor.
neurips-2023-on-the-generalization-error.tldr: A direct supermartingale analysis sharpens stochastic mirror descent generalization bounds across independent, dependent, light-tailed, and heavy-tailed data settings.

paragraphs: SEEG provides detailed recordings of brain activity for seizure detection, but a model must cope with substantial differences between patients and between brain areas. PPi addresses these two sources of variation through pretraining and domain-generalization techniques. Its aim is seizure detection that can work across patients while retaining meaningful regional differences in brain signals.

The model uses two self-supervised tasks to learn from abundant SEEG data. These tasks are designed to extract useful information without erasing the distinctive characteristics of signals recorded in different brain regions. The authors then introduce channel background subtraction and brain region enhancement to address shifts between patients. Together, these components connect broad signal learning with explicit treatment of the variation that complicates transfer.

Experiments on two public datasets and an additional clinical dataset collected by the authors show improvements over state-of-the-art baselines. Visualization analysis also supports the rationale for the two domain-generalization techniques. The reported evidence establishes effectiveness across those evaluated datasets and supports the practical promise of combining region-sensitive pretraining with methods aimed at patient-to-patient variation.
neurips-2023-ppi-pretraining-brain-signa.tldr: PPi combines self-supervised SEEG pretraining with domain-generalization techniques to improve seizure detection across patients in three evaluated datasets.

paragraphs: Federated learning and analytics must balance accurate aggregate estimates against privacy requirements and communication costs. This paper studies that balance through mean and frequency estimation under differential privacy. Its central idea is that communicating a randomly selected part of each client's information can both reduce message size and amplify privacy.

The authors develop two versions. In the central privacy model, the random selection is revealed to the server. In the second, a secure shuffler mixes clients' selected data parts, producing a multi-message shuffled privacy guarantee. Both constructions achieve the stated optimal trade-offs among privacy, communication, and accuracy. The difference is how the selected information reaches the server and which privacy framework applies.

For optimal squared-Euclidean-error performance, the authors show that per-client communication of order n min(ε, ε²) bits is sufficient for mean estimation, and logarithmic in that quantity for frequency estimation. These are sufficiency results, with n denoting client count. Compared with uncompressed communication tied to dimension or domain size d, substantial savings arise when n min(ε, ε²) is asymptotically smaller than d.
neurips-2023-privacy-amplification-via-c.tldr: Randomly selecting and compressing client information achieves optimal privacy–accuracy–communication trade-offs for private mean and frequency estimation.

paragraphs: Temporal graphs represent relationships that evolve over time, but gathering information from every past neighbor can be computationally expensive. A common shortcut uses only the most recent neighbors. That shortcut makes the information available to a node incomplete and biased toward recent interactions, potentially overlooking relevant parts of its history.

This paper proposes a different neighbor-aggregation framework based on recurrent neural networks. Each node has its own hidden state, which integrates information from all of its historical neighbors. The framework therefore makes accumulated history part of the node's evolving representation instead of limiting aggregation to a recent subset. This directly addresses the particular information loss introduced by subsampling historical neighbors.

The authors establish superior theoretical expressiveness for the proposed framework and report state-of-the-art performance in real-world applications. A highlighted result is a 9.4% improvement in average precision over existing methods on an e-commerce dataset using two-layer models. The theoretical and empirical findings together support retaining historical neighbor information through recurrent state as a useful design for temporal graph learning.
neurips-2023-recurrent-temporal-revision.tldr: Node-specific recurrent states integrate all historical neighbors, improving temporal graph expressiveness and reported real-world prediction performance.

paragraphs: Balanced-tree recursive networks process long sequences efficiently because their recursion depth grows logarithmically with sequence length. However, their fixed composition structure struggles with structure-sensitive tasks such as ListOps. More flexible recursive models can solve these tasks but demand much more time and memory. Recursion in Recursion, or RIR, combines the two approaches.

RIR uses a balanced k-ary tree as its outer recursion and a Beam Tree recursive network inside each cell. A proposed beam-alignment strategy adapts the inner model to this arrangement. The resulting total recursive depth is bounded above by k log base k of n. This architecture retains a scalable outer organization while allowing richer composition within its individual recursive operations.

The best RIR model achieves at least 90% length-generalization performance on ListOps while remaining trainable on long Long Range Arena inputs. It can reduce the original Beam Tree model's memory use by hundreds of times. On LRA language tasks it is competitive with structured state-space models and substantially outperforms Transformers. State-space models can slightly surpass it on LRA, but fail the reported ListOps length-generalization test.
neurips-2023-recursion-in-recursion-two-.tldr: RIR nests flexible recursion inside a balanced tree to combine strong ListOps length generalization with scalable long-sequence processing.

paragraphs: Operator learning aims to learn mappings between functions, including mappings associated with partial differential equations. The mathematical description can live in an infinite-dimensional function space, but a computer must work with a discrete representation. This translation can change what the model actually computes, creating a mismatch between the intended operator and its implementation.

The Representation equivalent Neural Operators framework, or ReNO, makes that mismatch a central object of study. It introduces operator aliasing as a measure of inconsistency between a neural operator and its discrete representations. The authors investigate this issue in widely used operator-learning techniques, connecting their computational representations to the continuous objects they are meant to approximate.

Their findings explain how aliasing can introduce errors when models handle different grids or discretizations, and how it can remove important continuous structure. This makes representation consistency a concrete concern for assessing neural operators across computational settings. The framework is also constructive and broad, which the authors identify as a potential source of tools for designing new operators. That design opportunity is presented as a possibility, alongside the analysis of existing methods.
neurips-2023-representation-equivalent-n.tldr: ReNO formalizes inconsistencies between neural operators and their discretizations, explaining grid-dependent errors and potentially guiding new operator designs.

paragraphs: When the distribution of operating conditions changes, a decision that looked good under a reference distribution may become unreliable. Robust satisficing addresses this by seeking robustness to an unspecified distributional shift while maintaining utility above a desired threshold. This paper brings that objective into contextual Bayesian optimization with noisy black-box evaluations.

The proposed RoBOS algorithm handles a discrepancy between the true distribution of context and the reference distribution used for optimization. Its goal is organized around meeting a desired level of utility under distributional uncertainty. This gives the optimization problem a threshold-based notion of success, alongside the need to learn from noisy observations of an unknown objective.

The authors prove sublinear lenient regret under assumptions about the amount of distribution shift. They also introduce a weaker measure, robust satisficing regret, and prove a sublinear upper bound that is independent of the shift amount. The distinction matters: the shift-independent statement uses the weaker criterion. Applications to several learning problems and comparisons with approaches including distributionally robust optimization are used to demonstrate the method's effectiveness.
neurips-2023-robust-bayesian-satisficing.tldr: RoBOS targets satisfactory utility under context-distribution shifts, with conditional lenient-regret guarantees and a shift-independent bound for a weaker regret measure.

paragraphs: Federated learning becomes harder when the data encountered after training differ from the training domains. Domain-generalization methods seek to handle that shift, but each federated client may have too few examples or too little domain variety to apply them effectively. StableFDG addresses both local diversity and the learning of characteristics shared across domains.

Its first component expands the styles a client can learn from through style sharing, shifting, and exploration. This allows training to consider styles beyond those originally present in the client's data. Its second component is an attention-based feature highlighter. It compares features of examples from the same class and emphasizes their important common characteristics, helping the model learn class information that is less tied to a particular domain.

The two components address complementary difficulties: restricted exposure to variation and limited evidence about what should remain stable across that variation. Experiments show that StableFDG outperforms existing baselines on multiple domain-generalization benchmarks. These results support the combination of style diversity and attention to shared class features in the evaluated federated settings with limited local data.
neurips-2023-stablefdg-style-and-attenti.tldr: StableFDG combines expanded style diversity with attention to shared class features to improve federated generalization across domains.

paragraphs: Unsupervised anomaly detectors must distinguish ordinary data from unexpected behavior without labels that directly validate their decision boundaries. Their heuristic boundaries can therefore produce uncertain predictions, especially for nearby examples. Allowing a detector to reject uncertain cases offers one response, but choosing both a confidence measure and a rejection threshold without labels is difficult.

This paper uses a stability metric computed by ExCeeD and applies a constant rejection threshold to it. The choice is supported by a theoretical analysis of the metric. The method thus turns rejection into a rule grounded in the behavior of an existing stability measure, addressing both how to express confidence and how to decide which predictions to withhold.

The analysis estimates the test-time rejection rate and derives upper bounds for both that rate and expected prediction cost. These guarantees help characterize the consequences of permitting rejection, beyond simply improving confidence in retained predictions. Experiments show that the method outperforms some other metric-based approaches. The stated comparison is selective, while the theoretical contribution provides explicit control over aspects of rejection behavior.
neurips-2023-unsupervised-anomaly-detect.tldr: A constant threshold on ExCeeD stability enables unsupervised anomaly-detection rejection with bounds on rejection rate and expected prediction cost.

paragraphs: Metal implants complicate CT reconstruction because metal attenuates different X-ray energies very differently. This creates nonlinear effects in the measurements. Polyner treats metal artifact reduction as a nonlinear inverse problem, addressing the physical acquisition process rather than relying on the empirical models that the authors associate with signal loss and aliased reconstructions.

The method first derives a polychromatic forward model that simulates CT acquisition across X-ray energies. It incorporates that model into an implicit neural representation used for reconstruction. A regularizer then constrains the possible solutions while preserving physical properties across energy levels. These components combine a learned image representation with a model of how the metal-affected measurements arise.

Polyner is unsupervised and needs no external training data. Across multiple datasets, it achieves comparable or better results than supervised methods on in-domain data and substantial improvements on out-of-domain data. The authors qualify their priority claim as being, to their knowledge, the first unsupervised metal artifact reduction method to outperform supervised counterparts. The reported comparisons support the value of modeling acquisition physics when reconstructing scans outside familiar data domains.
neurips-2023-unsupervised-polychromatic-.tldr: Polyner combines a polychromatic CT model with a neural representation to reduce metal artifacts without external training data.

paragraphs: Single-cell RNA sequencing produces large collections of records, each measuring expression across many genes. Learning useful representations from these data is attractive, but classical Transformers can require prohibitive computation and memory. xTrimoGene addresses that scaling problem by designing its architecture around the sparse structure of single-cell expression data.

The model uses an asymmetric Transformer encoder and decoder for unsupervised representation learning. Its sparse-data design reduces FLOPs by one to two orders of magnitude relative to classical Transformers while maintaining high accuracy. This makes larger-scale pretraining feasible. The authors describe the resulting models and training dataset as the largest in this setting at the time of their work.

Experiments show that performance improves as model size increases. The learned representations also yield reported state-of-the-art results on downstream tasks including cell-type annotation, perturb-seq effect prediction, and drug-combination prediction. These findings connect architectural efficiency to useful biological prediction: reducing the cost of ingesting sparse expression records enables scaling that, in the experiments, improves both representation learning and subsequent task performance.
neurips-2023-xtrimogene-an-efficient-and.tldr: xTrimoGene exploits sparse gene-expression data to scale Transformer pretraining efficiently and improve several downstream biological prediction tasks.
